newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-PSV THRASH FEYENOORD 7-2 TO TOP TABLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSV THRASH FEYENOORD 7-2 TO TOP TABLE.

text.p: PSV Eindhoven thrashed Feyenoord Rotterdam 7-2 on Sunday to regain the lead in the Dutch first division in a match packed with drama and goals.
PSV went into the match shaken by their 2-1 European Cup Winners' Cup defeat against Norwway's Brann Bergen and missing goalkeeper Ronald Waterreus and skipper Arthur Numan through suspension.
In contrast, Feyenoord had been playing superbly, and enjoyed a 3-0 away win against Spain's Espanyol in the UEFA Cup on Tuesday.
The Rotterdammers scored the first and last goals of the match, but the rest of the evening belonged to PSV.
Feyenoord went ahead through Swede Henke Larsson after only 71 seconds, but the home side refused to panic and patiently sought holes in an initially well organized Rotterdam defence.
The visitors were not helped by losing midfielder Jean-Paul van Gastel with a knee injury after 30 minutes and Pablo Sanchez with a hamstring strain minutes later.
It took PSV 37 minutes to open their account, Wim Jonk rounding off a stylish move after back-heels from Marciano Vink and Rene Eykelkamp wrong-footed their opponents.
But the turning point of the match came a minute before half time when Feyenoord defender George Boateng clattered Philip Cocu in the penalty area and was sent off.
Luc Nilis scored from the resulting spot-kick -- his eighth goal of the season.

Feyenoord never recovered their shape once they were a man down and in the second half PSV ran riot. Cocu scored twice and Boudewijn Zenden, Boudewijn Pahlplatz and Belgian Marc Degryse grabbed one apiece to make the score 7-1.
The visitors managed a goal in the last minute but PSV jump to the top of the table with 24 points from 11 games, one point ahead of Feyenoord.
Champions Ajax Amsterdam continued their poor results and needed an equaliser six minutes from time against lowly Volendam to save them from their first league defeat at their new Arena stadium.
Volendam withstood waves of Ajax attacks throughout the first hour and then scored on the break through Gert Aandewiel after 66 minutes.
Ajax struck back through defender Winston Bogarde, who latched onto a cross from forward Patrick Kluivert, back in the side after two months sidelined through injury.
The 1995 European champions are sixth and trail PSV by seven points.
